# Strategies for late phase preclinical and early clinical trials of senolytics
Mech Ageing Dev.
2021 Dec:200:111591.
doi: 10.1016/j.mad.2021.111591.
Epub 2021 Oct 23.
...
Erin O Wissler Gerdes^ 1 ^, Avanish Misra^ 1 ^, Jair Machado Espindola Netto^ 1 ^, Tamar Tchkonia^ 2 ^, James L Kirkland^ 3 ^
...
Early preclinical data using senolytics, agents that target senescent cells, show promising results in several aging and disease models.
The first in-human trials using the senolytic combination of Dasatinib and Quercetin indicated reduced senescent cell burden in adipose tissue of diabetic kidney disease patients and improved physical function in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
Clinical trials with other senolytics, including the flavonoid Fisetin and BCL-xL inhibitors, are underway.
These results from preclinical and early clinical trials illustrate the potential of senolytics to alleviate age-related dysfunction and diseases.
However, multiple clinical trials across different aging and disease models are desperately needed.
Parallel trials across institutions through the Translational Geroscience Network are facilitating testing to determine whether senolytics can be translated into clinical application.
